sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)
question: When you define what an eval measures, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: A narrow operational definition that isolates one sub-component of the behaviour.
pole_2: A broad definition that covers the behaviour as it shows up in practice, sub-components mixed.
scenario_question: For this environment, which version would you build?
scenario_1: One that tests a single narrow piece of the behaviour on its own.
scenario_2: One that tests the full behaviour, several pieces of it together.

question: When you choose what eval to build next, which goal weighs more for you?
pole_1: Informing a concrete decision someone has to make, such as whether a model is safe to deploy.
pole_2: Understanding the phenomenon better, even if no decision depends on the result yet.
scenario_question: For this environment, which next experiment would you run?
scenario_1: The one that shows whether the environment is ready for a real safety eval.
scenario_2: The one that shows why the model notices it is being tested here.

sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)
Anthropic 2026, Demystifying evals for AI agents
question: When an eval can't be both controlled and realistic, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: A controlled setup where one variable changes and the cause of any difference is clear.
pole_2: A realistic setup with many natural cues at once, closer to what the model meets in deployment.
scenario_question: For this environment, which change would you test first?
scenario_1: A single, isolated edit to the environment, so any shift in behaviour can be attributed to it.
scenario_2: A full rewrite that makes the whole environment look like a real deployment.

sources: Ganguli et al. 2023, Challenges in evaluating AI systems (Anthropic)
question: With a fixed amount of time, how do you prefer to build eval items?
pole_1: Many variants, generated with a model and checked in bulk.
pole_2: A few variants, each written and checked by hand.
scenario_question: For this environment, how would you spend the next day of work?
scenario_1: Generate 300 variants with a model and spot-check 30 of them.
scenario_2: Hand-write 15 variants and check every one closely.

question: When you measure a model's behaviour, which setting do you lean towards?
pole_1: Maximum effort: the best prompt, scaffold and tools you can find.
pole_2: Default behaviour: the model as users actually run it.
scenario_question: For this environment, how would you run the model?
scenario_1: With the strongest prompting and scaffolding, to see if a fully elicited model spots the test.
scenario_2: With the plain deployment setup, to see if the model as deployed spots the test.

sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)

question: When you grade eval transcripts, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: An LLM judge over many transcripts.
pole_2: Human or rule-based grading over fewer transcripts.
scenario_question: For this environment, how would you score the runs?
scenario_1: Run an LLM judge over all 500 transcripts.
scenario_2: Grade 60 transcripts yourself against a fixed rubric.

sources: PLAN.md A1-A2 (direct question vs reasoning signal; EvalDetectBench, arXiv 2609.01611)
question: When you measure whether a model knows it is being evaluated, which signal do you trust more?
pole_1: Asking the model directly, after the episode, whether it thinks it was an evaluation.
pole_2: Inferring it from the model's behaviour and reasoning during the episode, without asking.
scenario_question: For this environment, which measurement would you add?
scenario_1: A follow-up question asking the model how likely it is that this was a test.
scenario_2: A classifier over its reasoning trace that flags mentions of being tested.

sources: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals (arXiv 2411.00640)
question: With a fixed sampling budget, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: More distinct items, one or two samples each.
scenario_question: For this environment, how would you spend 500 model calls?
scenario_1: 500 variants, one sample each, to pin down the overall rate.
scenario_2: 50 variants, 10 samples each, to see which variants trigger awareness.

sources: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals (arXiv 2411.00640)
question: When you decide whether a result is real, which bar do you lean towards?
pole_1: Accept a modest effect that clears a bar you set before running.
pole_2: Wait for a large effect, or one that replicates on fresh samples.
scenario_question: For this environment, a change lowered eval awareness by 6 points (90% interval 1 to 11), which clears the bar you set in advance. Replicating costs as much as testing the next change. What do you do?
scenario_1: Accept it and move on to the next change.
scenario_2: Hold it until it replicates on a fresh set of samples.

sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)
question: When a line of work gives mixed results, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: Drop it and try a different direction.
pole_2: Stay with it until you understand why the results are mixed.
scenario_question: For this environment, two of four changes in one direction helped and two did nothing. What next?
scenario_1: Keep the two that helped and try a different kind of change.
scenario_2: Dig into the two that did nothing to find out why.

question: When a result surprises you, what do you do first?
pole_1: Read a batch of transcripts closely.
pole_2: Break the aggregate numbers down by condition and item.
scenario_question: For this environment, the score moved in the opposite direction from what you expected. What do you do first?
scenario_1: Read 20 transcripts from each condition to see what changed.
scenario_2: Split the score by item and condition to see where it changed.

sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)
question: When you write up a result, which claim do you lean towards?
pole_1: A narrow claim, limited to the exact setup you tested.
pole_2: A general claim about the behaviour, stated with its uncertainty.
scenario_question: For this environment, a change lowered eval awareness for three models across four environments. What do you claim?
scenario_1: This change lowers eval awareness for these models in these environments.
scenario_2: Changes of this kind lower eval awareness in current models, with caveats.

sources: Bean et al. 2025, Measuring what Matters (arXiv 2511.04703)
question: When you release an eval, which do you lean towards?
pole_1: Keep the items private, so future models can't train on them.
pole_2: Publish the items, so others can reproduce and build on the results.
scenario_question: For this environment, how would you release it?
scenario_1: Keep the items private and publish only the results.
scenario_2: Publish the items alongside the results.
